screen1-a1.where: the three short lines in the top left corner
screen1-a1.expectation: I believe it opens a list of other places in the application, but that is a guess.
screen1-a1.cue: Nothing but the three lines themselves; there is no word beside them.

first_pass.why: Three lines are not a word. I cannot be certain what they do, and I cannot carry the answer from one screen to the next; each time I would have to press it to find out.
first_pass.solution: Put the word 'Menu' under or beside the three lines.

test_cases.targets: whether you can rely on the three lines meaning the same thing from screen to screen
test_cases.action: Start from the main screen (the one with the typing box at the bottom). If you are not there, press the three lines at the top left and then 'New chat'. Press the three lines at the top left. See what opens. Press 'Chats'. On that page press the three lines again. See what opens. Close with Back.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: you would still have to press it each time to find out what it does
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: once you have seen it you could rely on it without testing it again
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the three lines at the top left of the main screen. A list slid in from the left with the name 'Claude' at the top and the plain words Chats, Projects, Code and Artifacts beneath. I pressed 'Chats' and a page headed 'Chats' opened; there too the three lines were at the top left, and pressing them brought the very same list, with 'Chats' now shaded. Back closed it. I should add one thing I noticed: when I later started a new chat from the Chats page, the corner on the main screen showed an arrow instead of the three lines, so the corner is not always the same.

screen1-a1.closing_comment: It did the same thing every time, and what opens has words on it, so pressing it to find out costs me nothing. But I shall not remember the three lines, and the corner sometimes shows an arrow instead, so it still wants the word 'Menu'.

screen1-a2.where: the little ghost face in the top right corner
screen1-a2.expectation: I have no idea. A ghost means nothing to me in a telephone.
screen1-a2.cue: Nothing. There is only the drawing of a ghost, and no word.

first_pass.why: It is a picture I have never learned and cannot learn. I would not press it, or if I did I would not know what I had done.
first_pass.solution: Replace the ghost with plain words that say what it does, written on the button itself.

test_cases.targets: whether anything tells you what the ghost does before it changes the screen, or only afterwards
test_cases.action: Start from the main screen (the one with the typing box at the bottom). If you are not there, press the three lines at the top left and then 'New chat'. Hold your finger on the ghost at the top right for about a second and watch for any words. Then read what the screen now says. To go back, press the same corner control again.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: no words name it before anything changes, and you only find out what it did after it has done it
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: words appear (on holding, or near it) that tell you what it does before anything changes
test_cases.what_happened: On the main screen I held my finger on the ghost at the top right for about a second. No words appeared. Instead the screen changed while I was still holding it: the heading 'Incognito chat', a larger ghost and a sentence about chats staying out of my history appeared. The X in the top right corner took me back.

screen1-a2.closing_comment: Nothing named the ghost before it acted. I only learnt what it did after it had done it, and even holding my finger on it, which is how I would ask a question, set it off.

screen1-a3.expectation: It would take me to a page asking me to pay for a better version of the service.

first_pass.why: 'Upgrade' is an ordinary word. I know it means paying for more.

test_cases.targets: which kind of adding the plus does (a file, a new chat, a project)

test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not what you expected, or it still does not settle which kind of adding it is
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens matches what you expected and makes the plus's job clear

test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: it opens what you guessed (your account or settings)

screen33-a7.closing_comment: It is what I guessed — my account and settings. The heading says so clearly once I am there, but the circle itself still has no word, and next time I shall have to guess again.

screen33-a8.where: the black button '+ New chat' at the bottom right

first_pass.why: Plain words saying exactly what will happen.

screen34-a1.where: the three short lines in the top left corner
screen34-a1.expectation: I believe it opens a list of other places in the application, but that is a guess.
screen34-a1.cue: Nothing but the three lines themselves; there is no word beside them.

first_pass.why: Three lines are not a word. I cannot be certain what they do, and I cannot carry the answer from one screen to the next; each time I would have to press it to find out.
first_pass.solution: Put the word 'Menu' under or beside the three lines.

test_cases.targets: whether you can rely on the three lines meaning the same thing from screen to screen
test_cases.action: Start from the main screen (the one with the typing box at the bottom). If you are not there, press the three lines at the top left and then 'New chat'. test_cases.problem_is_real_if: you would still have to press it each time to find out what it does
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: once you have seen it you could rely on it without testing it again

I pressed 'Chats' and a page headed 'Chats' opened; there too the three lines were at the top left, and pressing them brought the very same list, with 'Chats' now shaded. Back closed it. screen34-a1.closing_comment: It did the same thing every time, and what opens has words on it, so pressing it to find out costs me nothing. But I shall not remember the three lines, and the corner sometimes shows an arrow instead, so it still wants the word 'Menu'.

screen34-a2.where: the X in the top right corner

screen34-a2.cue: The X, which I know means close, and the words 'Incognito chat' below it.

first_pass.why: I know X means close, but there is no box or popup here, the whole screen is the chat, so I am not sure what it closes or where I would land.
first_pass.solution: Write 'Leave incognito chat' next to the X.

test_cases.targets: what the X on the incognito screen closes, and whether what you had typed is kept or thrown away
test_cases.action: Start from the main screen (the one with the typing box at the bottom). If you are not there, press the three lines at the top left and then 'New chat'. test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the X plainly takes you back to the ordinary screen and you can tell what happened to your word
test_cases.what_happened: (same control as screen3-a2; the try was run once and applies here) I pressed the ghost so the 'Incognito chat' screen appeared, typed 'test' in the box without sending, and pressed the X at the top right. screen34-a2.closing_comment: The X did what I thought — it left the incognito chat and took me back to the ordinary screen — and it did not throw away what I had written. That is a fair outcome and my worry does not hold.

screen34-a3.where: the underlined words 'Learn more' in the middle
screen34-a3.expectation: It would explain what an incognito chat is.

first_pass.why: Plain words, and they sit right under the explanation they belong to.

screen34-a6.where: the round button with a plus sign at the bottom left
screen34-a6.expectation: It adds something, but I cannot say what — a new chat, a picture, a file?

test_cases.targets: which kind of adding the plus does (a file, a new chat, a project)

test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not what you expected, or it still does not settle which kind of adding it is
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens matches what you expected and makes the plus's job clear

screen34-a6.closing_comment: It is adding a picture or a document, as I half guessed, and the heading 'Add to chat' says so plainly once it is open. I still have to press it to find that out, because the plus has no word.

screen34-a7.where: the grey pill saying 'Haiku 4.5' at the bottom
screen34-a7.expectation: I have no idea. A haiku is a Japanese poem. Perhaps it writes a poem for me?
screen34-a7.cue: The words 'Haiku 4.5', which are a name, not an instruction.

first_pass.why: It is an invented name with a number. I cannot learn what it stands for, so it is a wall to me.
first_pass.solution: Say what it does in ordinary words, for example 'Choose how the assistant answers: quick or careful', and keep that wording the same everywhere.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the 'Haiku 4.5' pill shows what it is and that it is something you can change
test_cases.action: Start from the main screen (the one with the typing box at the bottom). If you are not there, press the three lines at the top left and then 'New chat'. test_cases.problem_is_real_if: you still cannot tell what 'Haiku 4.5' is or what changing it would do
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens tells you plainly what the pill is for

I chose nothing and closed it with the X.

screen34-a7.closing_comment: Now I can see it is a choice and that the descriptions talk about speed and difficulty. But 'model' is never explained, and the name on the pill itself still tells me nothing when I look at it again.

screen34-a8.where: the grey round button with a microphone at the bottom right

test_cases.targets: whether the round black button with bars could be the send button, and whether anything tells it apart from the microphone

test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the screen shows you plainly what the black button is for, or which button sends

first_pass.why: The words say exactly what happens.
